ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a blue discrete-time feedback system block diagram. Input X enters the positive terminal of the first summing point on the left, and the signal at the output end is fed back along the bottom to the negative terminal of that summing point; after the first summing point is connected gain K. After gain K, it enters the second summing point; the internal signal output by the second summing point goes to the right, and at the same time goes downward into the delay module. The delay output returns to the input of the second summing point through the lower path and gain 10. There is also a summing point on the right, which adds the signal on the output path of the second summing point and the path related to the delay output to obtain output Y. Reasoning: According to the specified method, let the output of the second summing point be A, and the delay output be D. From the structure in the figure, write E = X - Y, U = K E, D = z^{-1}A, A = U + 10D, Y = A + D. Substituting D = z^{-1}A and U = K(X - Y), there is A = K(X - Y) + 10z^{-1}A, and Y = (1 + z^{-1})A. After eliminating A, obtain the transfer function Y/X = K(1 + z^{-1}) / [1 - 10z^{-1} + K(1 + z^{-1})]. Therefore the characteristic denominator is (1 + K) + (K - 10)z^{-1}. Set the denominator to zero and multiply by z to obtain the pole z = (10 - K)/(1 + K). Because the system requires causal stability, the pole must be inside the unit circle, so |(10 - K)/(1 + K)| < 1. Simplifying gives (10 - K)^2 < (1 + K)^2, that is 2K - 9 > 0, therefore K > 4.5.

method.method_draft: Let q[n] be the output of the delay block, so q[n+1] equals the signal A[n] at the output of the second summer. From the diagram, the output is Y[n]=A[n]+q[n]. The second summer gives A[n]=K(X[n]-Y[n])+10q[n] because the outer feedback subtracts Y at the first summer and the gain-10 path adds the delayed state. Substitute Y[n]=A[n]+q[n] into A[n]=K(X[n]-A[n]-q[n])+10q[n]. Solve for A[n]: (1+K)A[n]=KX[n]+(10-K)q[n]. Therefore q[n+1]=A[n]=[K/(1+K)]X[n]+[(10-K)/(1+K)]q[n]. The closed-loop eigenvalue is (10-K)/(1+K); causal stability requires its magnitude below 1, so K>4.5.
